paper_title: Improving Active Layer Morphology of All-Polymer Solar Cells by Dissolving the Two Polymers Individually

qa_pairs.question: What is the fundamental difference between the DI (Dissolving Individually) and DT (Dissolving Together) methods in the fabrication of all-polymer solar cells?
qa_pairs.answer: The DI method involves dissolving the polymer donor and polymer acceptor in separate solutions and mixing them immediately before spin-coating. In contrast, the conventional DT method involves dissolving both the polymer donor and acceptor in the same solution simultaneously to create a well-intermixed blend.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improving Active Layer Morphology of All-Polymer Solar Cells by Dissolving the Two Polymers Individually

qa_pairs.question: For an all-polymer solar cell using J61 as the donor and PBN-10 as the acceptor, what were the power conversion efficiency (PCE) and open-circuit voltage (VOC) achieved using the DI method?
qa_pairs.answer: The J61:PBN-10 based all-polymer solar cell achieved a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 7.09% and an open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 1.24 V when processed using the DI method.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improving Active Layer Morphology of All-Polymer Solar Cells by Dissolving the Two Polymers Individually

qa_pairs.question: What are the LUMO and HOMO energy levels for the donor polymer J61 and the acceptor polymer PBN-10?
qa_pairs.answer: The LUMO and HOMO energy levels for the donor J61 are -3.08 eV and -5.32 eV, respectively. For the acceptor PBN-10, the LUMO level is -3.42 eV and the HOMO level is -5.81 eV.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improving Active Layer Morphology of All-Polymer Solar Cells by Dissolving the Two Polymers Individually

qa_pairs.question: How does the DI method physically improve the active layer morphology of all-polymer solar cells compared to the DT method?
qa_pairs.answer: The DI method leverages the low diffusion coefficient of long polymer chains. Because the polymers are mixed immediately before spin-coating, the pre-formed aggregates in the individual solutions do not have enough time to deaggregate or intermix completely. This allows the solution-state aggregation to be partially preserved in the resulting thin film, leading to improved morphology.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improving Active Layer Morphology of All-Polymer Solar Cells by Dissolving the Two Polymers Individually

qa_pairs.question: How does the DI processing method affect the charge carrier mobilities of the J61:PBN-10 blend relative to the DT method?
qa_pairs.answer: The DI method significantly improves both hole and electron mobilities. Specifically, the hole mobility (μh) increases from 6.05 × 10⁻⁵ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ (DT) to 1.83 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ (DI), and the electron mobility (μe) increases from 3.16 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ (DT) to 5.88 × 10⁻⁴ cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ (DI).
qa_pairs.source_title: Improving Active Layer Morphology of All-Polymer Solar Cells by Dissolving the Two Polymers Individually

qa_pairs.question: According to 2D-GIWAXS analysis, how does the DI method influence the structural ordering and coherence length of the J61:PBN-10 blend?
qa_pairs.answer: The DI method enhances polymer ordering, as evidenced by an increase in coherence length (CL). The CL of the (100) lamellar peak increases from 101 Å to 122 Å, and the (010) π–π stacking peak increases from 34 Å in the DT-processed film to 36 Å in the DI-processed film.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improving Active Layer Morphology of All-Polymer Solar Cells by Dissolving the Two Polymers Individually

qa_pairs.question: What impact does the DI method have on the relative domain purity of the J61:PBN-10 active layer as measured by Resonant soft X-ray scattering (R-SoXS)?
qa_pairs.answer: The R-SoXS measurements indicate that the DI method significantly increases the relative domain purity of the J61:PBN-10 active layer, raising it from 0.71 when using the DT method to 1.00 when using the DI method.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improving Active Layer Morphology of All-Polymer Solar Cells by Dissolving the Two Polymers Individually

qa_pairs.question: How do light-intensity-dependent short-circuit current (JSC) measurements demonstrate the advantage of the DI method in terms of charge collection and recombination?
qa_pairs.answer: The power-law exponent (α) derived from the measurements increases from 0.93 for the DT method to 0.95 for the DI method. A larger α value (closer to 1) suggests that free charge carriers are more efficiently swept out and collected by the electrodes prior to bimolecular recombination.
qa_pairs.source_title: Improving Active Layer Morphology of All-Polymer Solar Cells by Dissolving the Two Polymers Individually
